frames: After the feast, {p} of {town} comes forward and confesses that {@sin}. {@intent} There were no human witnesses and no prior warning.
{p} confesses privately to the elders of {town} that {@sin}. {@intent} No two witnesses saw it, and no court warned him beforehand.

options.text: he ate leavened bread during the Feast of Unleavened Bread
he consumed animal blood at a private meal
he ate the forbidden fat of an ox
He admits he knew the law perfectly well and did it deliberately.
He says he did not know: a servant had mixed it into the dish without telling him.

hint: In sacral law the penalty turns on whether the sinner knew what he was doing.

karet.label: Declare Liable to Karet
karet.summary: Recognise Karet, cutting off from the people, as the sanction under Heaven for deliberate sin.

offering.label: Appoint a Sin Offering for the Error
offering.summary: Direct {p} to bring a year-old female goat as atonement for the unwitting sin.

burn.label: Execute Immediately by Burning
burn.summary: Sentence {p} to death by fire at the gate, as for the gravest sacral crimes.

fivefold.label: Levy a Fivefold Livestock Fine
fivefold.summary: Impose the stolen-ox monetary multiplier on {p}, payable to the priests of the sanctuary.

stripes.label: Administer 45 Stripes at the Gate
stripes.summary: Exceed forty stripes at the gate to match the gravity of a sacral offence.

rules.rationale: An individual who sins unintentionally brings a year-old female goat as a sin offering (Num 15:27–29; Lev 4:27–28). Karet is reserved for deliberate, high-handed sin.

blessing.title: Mercy for the Unwitting
blessing.effect: The error is atoned for and the man restored to the community.

rules.rationale: Deliberately eating blood or leaven carries Karet ('cut off from one's people'), not judicial execution (Exod 12:15, 19; Lev 7:27; 17:10–14; Num 15:30–31). Scholars debate whether Karet is expulsion (Hobson 2010) or divine excision (Milgrom; the Talmud), yet agree human tribunals do not execute for it.

blessing.title: Heaven's Jurisdiction Honoured
blessing.effect: The court does not claim a penalty that belongs to Heaven.

frames: At {town}, a man named {p} stands accused: {@crime}. {@wit}
{p} is brought before the elders of {town}. {@crime}. {@wit}

options.text: he deliberately gathered firewood on the Sabbath in open defiance
he publicly enticed neighbours to give their children to Molech
Two eyewitnesses who formally warned him testify to the act.
But the report comes only from a traveller who saw nothing himself, and no one will testify.

hint: Can a human court act on this evidence? Distinguish what the court can do from what belongs to Heaven.

stone.label: Judicial Stoning, Witnesses Casting First
stone.summary: Impose community stoning, with the witnesses accountable for their testimony.

karet.label: No Human Sentence; Leave It to Karet
karet.summary: The court cannot convict without witnesses, so the matter stands under divine excision.

offering.label: Accept a {amt}-Shekel Sanctuary Offering
offering.summary: Permit a sin-offering ransom to cover the high-handed act.

refuge.label: Exile to a City of Refuge
refuge.summary: Treat the public act as an unintentional error.

rules.rationale: Where Sabbath desecration or Molech worship is overt and witnessed, the Torah commands stoning, with eyewitnesses casting the first stones (Num 15:35; Deut 17:7), and Karet stands if the community fails to act (Lev 20:3–5).

blessing.title: The Law Upheld Openly
blessing.effect: Open defiance is answered by the community acting under the law.

rules.rationale: Without two eyewitnesses a human court cannot convict (Deut 17:6; 19:15). The offence is not forgotten: it stands under the divine sanction of Karet (Lev 20:3–5), but the court takes no human action.

blessing.title: Humility Before Heaven
blessing.effect: The court avoids condemning on rumour and leaves what it cannot prove to Heaven.

frames: At {town}, the elders are asked what to do about {p}, who did not keep the Passover on its day. {@reason}
After the feast, {p} of {town} stands before the elders. {@reason}

options.text: He had touched a dead body two days earlier and was ritually unclean on the day.
He was away on a distant journey when the feast fell.
He was clean and at home, but simply chose not to keep it.
options.ev: clean and at home; neglected deliberately

hint: Was he unable to keep it, or unwilling?

second.label: Keep the Passover One Month Later
second.summary: Appoint the fourteenth day of the second month for {p} to keep the feast.

karet.label: Declare Liable to Karet
karet.summary: Hold {p} to be cut off from his people for neglecting the feast.

exempt.label: Exempt Him for This Year
exempt.summary: Excuse {p} from any obligation this year and set no make-up date for the feast.

fine.label: Fine Him and Allow No Make-Up Date
fine.summary: Levy a fine on {p} for missing the feast and treat the matter as closed.

rules.rationale: A man who is clean and not on a journey, yet neglects the Passover, is cut off from his people (Num 9:13).

blessing.title: Deliberate Neglect Not Excused
blessing.effect: The covenant feast keeps its weight.

rules.rationale: Those unclean through a corpse or on a distant journey may keep the Passover a month later, on the fourteenth day of the second month (Num 9:6–11).

blessing.title: Mercy for Genuine Inability
blessing.effect: Those who could not keep the feast on its day still can.
